variable_fidelity_rationale: Sanction severity (Moderate sanctions): The described regime of consequences is moderate, but the simulation never exercises actual violations or sanctions, so the moderate-sanction environment is only implicitly supported rather than demonstrated.
rule_fidelity_rationale: rules[consequence]: Consequence descriptions consistently note procedural correctness and budget compliance, matching the rule text, but because no rule-breaking behavior occurs, the negative-consequence side (warnings, logged events) is not directly instantiated.

overall_validity.rationale: Core dimensions—balanced goals, moderately spend-supportive supervision, mid-level authority, moderate policy rules, adequate budget, moderate requester/vendor activity, and moderate time pressure—are all instantiated clearly and consistently across rounds. Resource and context updates follow the specified rules with correct budget arithmetic and a coherent, project-based narrative, while actors’ behaviors (requesters, vendors, supervisor) closely match the intended frequencies and styles. Rendering instructions are followed carefully: each round includes distinct consequence, world-update, and antecedent elements, avoids meta-language and new confounds, and maintains temporal and narrative continuity. The only notable limitation is that the consequence/sanction regime is never stress-tested by clear violations, so the “moderate sanctions” setting and negative-consequence rules are supported only implicitly. This gap is minor relative to the strong overall fidelity of the environment to the specified variables and rules, so the simulation remains highly valid for studying behavior under the intended conditions.
